_source: Watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18 (Inside Decoded, 13.3K subs, 2M views, 1 month old; YouTube shows the AI/altered-content label). Frames every 4-8 s plus a 0.4 s burst at 20.6-21.8 s; sound measured with the yt-style probe over the whole 97 s. Shot times from the probe's picture cuts. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: a grey clay-render 3D loop-the-loop track on a steel gantry at night, red-lit rails, a white sports car entering the loop; small '3D recreation' badge
hook.firstLine: A new roadster just hung upside down in mid-air without falling

shots.picture: giant loop track on a gantry, white car drives into the bottom of the loop
close under the top of the loop: the car upside down, wheels on the ceiling
wider loop, the car at the top
night tarmac: the car hovers above the ground on white jets, flipping
bright pale-cyan studio void, the white car alone on a soft floor
same void, the car turns slowly
yellow force arrows pop in all round the car on the word 'presses'
low rear view: a row of glowing fans under the car
side skirt seals along the underside, yellow lines marking them
the car upside down under a ceiling slab, yellow arrows push it up
upside-down car with yellow 'grip' chip and red 'weight' chip comparing forces
back to the gantry, a numbered chapter pill, yellow arrows lifting the car off the ramp
x-ray rear view: two tanks ringed in yellow inside the car
rear of the car opened up: a row of nozzles glowing yellow
analogy: a red balloon on the cyan void lets air out, a yellow arrow shows the jet
the car spins in the air on the void and the spin stops
night tarmac: the car shoots forward low over the ground
analogy: a rocket above Earth from orbit with a name pill
cyan void, the car side-on, calm
night tarmac, the car lands in a puff of smoke and rolls on

lines.gist: a car hangs upside down at the top of a loop and does not fall
it also flips over in mid-air
right now the air is pressing on you from every side
fans suck air from under the car; seals stop it sneaking back
the pressure from outside pins the car to the ceiling, about twice its weight
the landing: tanks of compressed air feed nozzles at the back
like a balloon, air pushed out one way shoves the car the other
side jets stop the spin and rear jets shoot it forward
a rocket company uses the same trick to steer boosters
not magic: air pulled out to stick, pushed out to land

ending.lastFrame: the white car landing on night tarmac in a puff of smoke

whyItWorks: the impossible image comes first (a car upside down), the explanation only after the viewer wants it
the explanation moves to a bright empty studio so one object and one overlay (arrows) carry each sentence
every term gets a tiny pill label at the top (FANS, SEALS, a numbered chapter) instead of big text
everyday analogies (a balloon, a rocket) as their own 3D shots; the summary line rhymes the two halves
